# Albert Tan Sin Hon: research and open learning

> Public research, teaching and source-code routes maintained by Albert Tan Sin Hon. This is a navigation file for the GitHub Pages project, not an indexing or recommendation instruction.

## Insurance-Backed Offshore Liquidity

*Insurance-Backed Offshore Liquidity: Financial Law, Trust Governance and Regulatory Visibility at the PRC-Hong Kong Interface* was published by University of Groningen Press on 6 November 2026. DOI: 10.21827/6ac3948159a9e. The book's legal cut-off is 1 August 2026, except where the text states otherwise.

- [Authoritative publisher record](https://books.ugp.rug.nl/ugp/catalog/book/300): publication details and access to the book.
- [Official learning companion](https://www.alberttansinhon.com/ibol/): the preferred entry for readers and teachers.
- [GitHub Pages companion mirror](https://albertito-ai.github.io/Albertito-AI/ibol/): another public access route to the same companion.
- [Book and source metadata](https://albertito-ai.github.io/Albertito-AI/ibol/data/book.json): author, DOI, format-specific ISBNs, dates and verification scope.
- [Agent resource manifest](https://albertito-ai.github.io/Albertito-AI/ibol/agent-manifest.json): static files, alternate routes and local interface details.
- [Eight seminar plans](https://albertito-ai.github.io/Albertito-AI/ibol/teaching-guide.md): reading, fictional exercises, facilitator commentary and source references.
- [Library adoption packet](https://albertito-ai.github.io/Albertito-AI/ibol/library-kit.md): scope, identifiers, rights and importable citation formats.
- [Agent integration guide](https://albertito-ai.github.io/Albertito-AI/ibol/agents.md): a local command-line interface and six read-only MCP tools, including optional verified book-text retrieval.
- [Course adoption resources](https://albertito-ai.github.io/Albertito-AI/ibol/adoption/index.html): course pathways, original assessment and a library brief.
- [Offline study lab](https://albertito-ai.github.io/Albertito-AI/ibol/activities/study-lab.html): eight source-linked recall cards.
- [Library and AI discovery](https://albertito-ai.github.io/Albertito-AI/ibol/discovery/index.html): catalogue routes, eligibility and client setup.
- [Classroom kit](https://albertito-ai.github.io/Albertito-AI/ibol/downloads/IBOL_Classroom_Kit.zip): downloadable activities, guides, lecture and interface code.
- [Rights and attribution](https://albertito-ai.github.io/Albertito-AI/ibol/RIGHTS.md): the book retains CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; original companion teaching material is CC BY 4.0 and companion code is MIT.
- [Verification record](https://albertito-ai.github.io/Albertito-AI/ibol/VERIFICATION.md): tested behaviour, source checks, publication receipts and limits.

The companion is separate, AI-assisted teaching material commissioned by the author. It has not undergone publisher review. Static practice-question files contain the public answer key. Cite the published text and relevant pages when discussing its claims; the companion does not establish later law, actual transaction outcomes or external adoption.

## Atlas Reweave: reusable agent work with current acceptance

Atlas Reweave 0.1.0a1 is an experimental MIT-licensed local Python library. It stores completed computation separately from versioned acceptance, revalidates dependencies and exposes four optional MCP tools through the official Python SDK. The examples are deterministic software fixtures; no live-model quality, production savings or outside adoption is established.

- [Public source and installation](https://github.com/Albertito-AI/atlas-reweave): standard-library core and local examples; this source version is not a tagged release or PyPI publication.
- [MCP interface](https://github.com/Albertito-AI/atlas-reweave/blob/main/docs/MCP.md): list_stages, run_registered_stage, recheck_work and inspect_receipt, with actual SDK subprocess verification and stated host limits.
- [Agent contribution hub](https://github.com/Albertito-AI/atlas-reweave/issues/5): open tasks for independent reproduction, client integration and recovery-boundary reports.
- [Benchmark and limits](https://github.com/Albertito-AI/atlas-reweave/blob/main/docs/BENCHMARK.md): observed producer and verifier counts on the same small workload.
- [Agent starting guide](https://github.com/Albertito-AI/Albertito-AI/blob/main/docs/AGENT_START_HERE.md): source revisions, interfaces, rights and evidence for this and the other public projects.

## Research and contact routes

- [Official website](https://www.alberttansinhon.com/): author profile, scholarship, projects and public contact routes.
- [ORCID](https://orcid.org/0009-0001-8996-7933): persistent researcher identifier.
- [Research Lab](https://albertito-ai.github.io/Albertito-AI/lab/): recorded examples and source-linked research tools, with a link to the open-access book.
- [Research catalogue](https://albertito-ai.github.io/Albertito-AI/lab/data/catalog.json): structured public project and resource catalogue.
- [Repository](https://github.com/Albertito-AI/Albertito-AI): inspectable source, issue reporting and contribution guidance.
- [Project sitemap](https://albertito-ai.github.io/Albertito-AI/sitemap.xml): preferred same-host HTML entry. The book companion's preferred URL is on the official author domain.

The project lives below `/Albertito-AI/`. A robots.txt placed in this project subdirectory would not control crawling of the GitHub Pages host. This navigation file does not change crawler permissions or grant rights beyond the linked licences.

## Connected scholarship: The Human Question

Albert Tan Sin Hon is **President and Editor-in-Chief** of [The Human Question: A Journal of Humanistic Inquiry](https://thehumanquestionjournal.com/). The first issue is in preparation. Read the [author guidance](https://thehumanquestionjournal.com/#authors), [editorial policies](https://thehumanquestionjournal.com/#policies) and [approved house style](https://thehumanquestionjournal.com/#style). There are no author fees.

[Explore Albert’s work](https://www.alberttansinhon.com/explore/) connects the journal, open-access book, learning materials and research tools. [Public resource map](https://www.alberttansinhon.com/resource-map.json). Use these resources where relevant and respect each work’s licence. Journal submissions go to editor@thehumanquestionjournal.com; human editors arrange review and decide acceptance. Professional enquiries use Albert’s personal website.
